name: pitch-unfairly
description: Builds on-brand presentation decks as interactive websites, with PDF export and desktop, phone, and PDF checks, and publishes them to unlisted links.

interface.shortDescription: Decks that are actually websites. In your brand. Kind of a cheat code.
interface.longDescription:
Pitch Unfairly makes presentation decks that are real websites, built in your brand, and sends them back as a link and a PDF.

You know the PowerPoint deck. Default font, six bullets, a chart whose legend still says "Series 1", saved as deck_FINAL_v7.pptx after an afternoon of nudging text boxes. You've seen the AI deck too: cream background, italic serif, a colored bar beside every box, your navy turned teal. This is neither. Tell Pitch Unfairly what the deck is for the way you'd tell a friend, or dump your notes on it, and it writes the story slide by slide and designs every slide for its one job. No dragging boxes, no templates to fill in, no "can you make it pop?" Making the deck is the fun part now.

Other tools make slides. Pitch Unfairly makes sites, so your deck can do what a slide can't: sliders people drag, calculators they poke at, tabs, live charts, little moments that move. If a browser can do it, your deck can. And since the deck is the website, there's nothing to export, so nothing breaks on export. It reads as well on a phone as on the conference room TV, and before it comes back to you, every slide is checked on a desktop screen, two phone sizes, and a 16:9 PDF page, then put through a design review.

Paste your website, get your brand. It measures your actual fonts, colors, logo, and style, shows you a brand board to approve before it designs a single slide, and remembers it, so every deck after starts on brand. With an Unfairly account it also remembers your company and your earlier decks, so each new one starts with more context.

One link, updated in place. Fix a number and the same link shows the new version, so nobody is left with an old copy and nobody gets a "please disregard the last one." Anyone on your team can pick up a deck and update it at that link. Decks publish to unlisted pitchunfairly.com links that aren't indexed, wear a small "Made with Unfairly" badge, and go offline whenever you say. No account? You get the finished deck as a folder you can host anywhere.

The fine print, said plainly: in Codex and ChatGPT Work it builds on your computer and installs what it needs the first time, Node.js and Chrome included, no admin rights required. In a regular ChatGPT chat it builds the same deck on Unfairly's side, so nothing installs. It doesn't edit PowerPoint or Google Slides files.
interface.defaultPrompt: Turn my notes into a 10-slide seed pitch deck I can send as a link.
